distinguishing_features: Introductory (pre-existing hardware retrofit): inserts a high-conductivity heat-spreader insert between ceramic and metal to equalize temperature, not a procedural duty-cycle setpoint change
Addresses CTE-mismatch stress from thermal cycling (Δα·ΔT), not fouling spallation via deposit-wall CTE mismatch
Passive structural enhancement that reduces the local junction ΔT gradient, rather than an active thermal-shock excitation schedule
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Reduce local thermal stress concentration at a ceramic-metal junction caused by CTE mismatch under thermal cycling, so as to prevent crack initiation.
parsed.viable_reason: A high-conductivity insert that flattens the local ΔT gradient is physically sound and testable with strain gauges and AE, though its effectiveness at 5 mm scale is checkable via the stated kill criterion.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: Adding a heat spreader to reduce localized thermal gradients at a CTE-mismatched joint is a genuine conceptual departure from compliant mounting or thermal-shock-cleaning approaches, not a routine parameter tweak.
